segments.script: First, meaning. I read “I am afraid you do not like your pen” slowly and put it in my own words: As Darcy writes a letter, Miss Bingley tells him she is afraid he does not like his pen. Next, craft. I notice the fussy, attentive remark about a trivial object, one of many interruptions she makes while he writes. The strongest word is “afraid”: it is polite exaggeration, pretending concern over a pen to get his attention. Then, effect. What is Miss Bingley really doing when she worries about Darcy's pen? My answer: She is not worried about the pen; she is flattering Darcy and trying to draw him into conversation, and his short replies show her pursuit is unwelcome.
